messages.subject: multi-species data filters
parts:
Hello,

I apologize if this is a simple question, but I have spent considerable time reading the DISTANCE manual and haven’t found a solution yet. I completed simple 75m radius breeding bird point counts. There are 5 species worth analyzing, At the same time I uploaded the typical data using the import wizard, I brought in a column from the text file under “Observation” and named it “Species”. The species items in the column are CASP, HOLA, MODO, WEKI, and WEME and I made it a text layer. I want to run an analysis of all observations of CASP (for example) in order to fit the right detection function and find density and abundance.  I created a data filter that selected from the Observation layer with the following SQL command: Species = ‘CASP’.  In the Results I receive errors including the red line below:

Initializing

Making Data File

Making Data Selection Queries

Found selection criterion: {SELECT * FROM [lyrObservation] WHERE Species = 'CASP'}

** Error: Encountered a problem while executing the data creating query.  **

Analysis engine status 'Errors in engine interface - engine not started'

Run finished

I’m ready to complete my analysis. Is there something simple I am missing or forgetting? I would appreciate any ideas.

Thank you,

Kristen Linner

Graduate Research Assistant

Natural Resources Management

Texas Tech University

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] multi-species data filters
parts:
Kristen:

Thanks for sending along your project.  I have good news and bad news:

good news:  The species filter works fine.  I had expected problems with capitalisation of the name of the field on which you are filtering.  But that is not the case.  Either of the two that follow work fine for your project, resulting in the proper number (160) detections of this species:
Found selection criterion: {SELECT * FROM [lyrObservation] WHERE species = 'CASP'}
Found selection criterion: {SELECT * FROM [lyrObservation] WHERE Species = 'CASP'}

so that solves your original question.

bad news:  Distance reports that there are too many point transects in your project: note this summary at the beginning of the results:
 Effort        :    689.0000   
 # samples     :   689
 Width         :    75.00000   
 # observations:   160

You see the correct number of sightings reported, and even the correct maximum detection distance.  What is incorrect is the number of transects (called samples in the output).  This will of course lead to an incorrect estimate of density.  The cause of this error is your sorting of data by species before importing the data.  The consequence of this is that point transect 'C04' appears far too often (it appears once for each of your year*month*species combinations).  You will need to reorganise your raw data and re-import. 

The data set up needs to respect the survey design, in other words the data are organised according the design rather than according to what was seen during the survey.  If you desire an estimate for each month of the study, then I suggest you construct month*year as strata (all of the same size 774ha), point transects within strata as samples, and species in the observation layer as you have.  Sort your data by strata and points within strata.

Let us know if this explanation of the new data structure makes sense to you.

Hi Eric,

I attached the text data file. Here is a link to the distance project zip file: https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/101999337/Fivespp3.zip

Thank you for your help!

In my study area (shortgrass prairie) it is not illogical to assume similar vegetation structure and thus searcher efficiency over the years. Will including strata in my data setup make this impossible?

Thank you,

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] multi-species data filters
parts:
Kirsten:

Stratification does not make a global model (no strata effects) impossible; rather, it makes it possible for you to assess whether a stratum effect exists.  The need for stratum-specific detection functions then becomes framed in a model-selection context; contrast models with a stratum effect with models that do not have a stratum effect.
